title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page is part of Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets'. He works with pairs of sections σ, ρ of a form G of GL(2) over a base scheme S, with neither σ nor ρ scalar on any fibre. They are put in the normal form (45) of the next page: ρ0 = [[0,1],[v,w]] and σ0 = [[0,-1],[v',w']] with v' = -v and w' = 1-w. This reflects the constraint that ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ is regular unipotent. The aim is to characterise when the pair gives the modular-group relations σ^2 = -1 (order 2 in PGL2) and ρ^3 = -1 (order 3 in PGL2), i.e. PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3.

Traces and determinants in the normal form. Tr ρ = w and det ρ = -v. Tr σ = 1-w and det σ = v' = -v. The pair is therefore governed by the two parameters (v, w).

Hamilton–Cayley for σ (labelled (36) on this page).
- σ^2 - (Tr σ)σ + det σ = 0.
- If Tr σ = 0 and det σ = 1, then σ^2 = -1.
- Conversely, if σ^2 = -1, then (Tr σ)σ = (det σ - 1)·1. Since σ is non-scalar on every fibre, 1 and σ are locally a basis of a direct factor of M2(O_S). Hence Tr σ = 0 and det σ = 1.

Hamilton–Cayley for ρ, equation (37), gives (38) by the same argument: (Tr ρ = 1 and det ρ = 1) ⇔ ρ^2 - ρ + 1 = 0.

Then (39): ρ^2 - ρ + 1 = 0 ⇒ ρ^3 = -1, via the identity ρ^3 + 1 = (ρ+1)(ρ^2 - ρ + 1).

In the normal form, 'Tr σ = 0 and det σ = 1' is the same as w = 1, v = -1, which is the same as Tr ρ = det ρ = 1. So all the conditions (27) are equivalent to a single quadratic relation on ρ. This is 'Corollaire 2', which as written states (40) ρ^2 + ρ + 1 = 0; by (38) the intended relation is ρ^2 - ρ + 1 = 0.

Relation to the previous page. There he had claimed the converse ρ^3 = -1 ⇒ ρ^2 - ρ + 1 = 0 using 'ρ+1 invertible', and crossed it out as 'faux'. Here he states only the implication (39). Combined with the previous page's corollary (any two of det ρ = 1, Tr ρ = 1, ρ^3 = -1 imply the third), the picture is consistent. In characteristic 3, ρ = -(1+N) with N^2 = 0 still satisfies all three relations, so nothing breaks.
errors: Corollaire 2, formula (40), reads ρ^2+ρ+1=0. By (38) it must be ρ^2-ρ+1=0, since Tr ρ = 1 and ρ^3 = -1. ρ^2+ρ+1=0 would correspond to Tr ρ = -1 and ρ^3 = 1. This is a sign slip.
Equation numbers (36) and (37) are reused from the crossed-out passage on the previous page, where (36) was the cubic identity. This is minor bookkeeping only.
The converse σ^2=-1 ⇒ (Tr σ = 0, det σ = 1) needs 1 and σ to be linearly independent fibrewise, i.e. σ to generate with 1 a direct summand. He correctly invokes this using non-scalarity on fibres.

ideas.what: Using Cayley–Hamilton plus fibrewise non-scalarity to turn the order relations σ^2=-1 and ρ^3=-1 in GL2 into trace/determinant conditions over a base scheme
ideas.modern_name: Cayley–Hamilton characterisation of elliptic elements of order 4 and 6 in SL2; trace conditions for PSL2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (folklore linear algebra; trace coordinates of SL2 representations à la Fricke–Klein)

ideas.what: Normal form of the pair (ρ, σ) with ρ0=[[0,1],[v,w]], σ0=[[0,-1],[-v,1-w]] encoding the condition that -σ^{-1}ρ is unipotent
ideas.modern_name: Companion-matrix normal form for 2-generator subgroups / modular-group representations into GL2 over a base
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 'Longue Marche' material on the modular group; unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Routine 2×2 linear algebra (Cayley–Hamilton) in service of the modular-group relations; the only notable feature is a sign slip in (40).
transcription_corrections: The superscript '466' at the top is Grothendieck's own page numbering, not part of the text.
The insertion above 'linéairement indépendantes' appears to read 'des sections' rather than 'des scalaires': '1 et σ sont des sections linéairement indépendantes en M_2(O_S)'.
In (36) the leading term is σ^2, written over a ρ, and the right-hand side is '= 0', overwritten.
'et [-relation-] l'implication': the crossed-out word looks like 'leur relation' (partly 'l'?); the reading 'et l'implication' stands.
